# Gobstopper

> Gobstopper makes long Claude Code and Codex sessions smaller. Preview each cut, write a compacted copy, and keep every original byte in a local vault.

Long coding-agent sessions collect tool output that mattered once: test logs from runs that have since passed, file listings from before a refactor, stack traces for bugs already fixed. Every turn sends all of it to the model again. Gobstopper is a free, open-source command-line tool that finds your Claude Code and Codex sessions, shows what each compaction strategy would cut, and writes a smaller copy. Before it writes, it stores the original bytes in a content-addressed vault on your machine, so you can search for the exact record a compaction left out or restore the whole session.

The source build also runs a local proxy that compacts live Claude Code and Codex requests and keeps direct provider-store edits and automatic provider compaction disabled.

When to use this site:
- Use gobstopper.sh to learn what Gobstopper does, which strategies it runs, and how to install it.
- Use /docs for the full reference: installation, strategies, configuration, the watcher, hooks, the snapshot vault, and the MCP server.
- Use /methodology for the occupancy model behind the projections and what each strategy does.
- Use /benchmarks for dated results, cohort sizes, limitations, and aggregate downloads.
- Use /compare/cliffcompaction to see how Gobstopper and its proxy compare with CliffCompaction, the API-proxy compactor, and what the cliff strategy does.
- Use /blog for longer posts on what Gobstopper does and how its archive and edit limits are checked.

## Pages

- [Gobstopper](https://gobstopper.sh/): what Gobstopper does, how to install it, and what it will not do to a running session.
- [Gobstopper documentation](https://gobstopper.sh/docs): the README, with every command, strategy, and configuration setting it documents.
- [Gobstopper methodology](https://gobstopper.sh/methodology): the occupancy model, the strategies, and the limits of the published benchmarks.
- [Gobstopper benchmarks](https://gobstopper.sh/benchmarks): offline replays of 729 archived sessions, a synthetic snapshot-recovery study, and historical single-session resume trials.
- [Gobstopper compared with CliffCompaction](https://gobstopper.sh/compare/cliffcompaction): where each tool runs, what each keeps and drops, what evidence each publishes, gobstopper proxy, which ports CliffCompaction's rule for Claude Code and Codex, and the cliff strategy for transcript copies.
